label: copy-phase echo of "i" as one of the first two original tokens
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input is the letter i and that i is an early original token: the input right after <DEL> (i was original token 0, recall_idx 1) or the next one (i was original token 1, recall_idx 2). Magnitude is strongly position-graded: i as the first original token gives the largest activations (~0.8-1.0 of max, 78% of mass); i as the second token gives ~0.1-0.35 of max; i as the third token (recall_idx 3) gives occasional weak activations (lowest quartile, the main source of missed recall). Never fires on i in the original phase, on <DEL>, on any other token, or on later-position copies of i. Output token and sequence length barely matter.

issues: The reported test scores reproduce exactly: precision 0.996, recall 0.902, F1 0.947, mass recall 0.993.

The phase claims hold. On dev, 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase, with 0 activations in the original phase or on <DEL>. in_tok == i carries 100% of the mass; only about 5 stray activations fall on r, z or k.

The recall_idx breakdown holds. recall_idx 1 gives precision 1.0 and 78.5% of mass, with top activations at 0.99-1.00 of max and third-quartile examples at 0.83-0.88. recall_idx 2 gives precision 0.993 and 20.7% of mass, with examples at about 0.1-0.33. recall_idx 3 fires on 22% of its steps with only 0.7% of mass. That weak tail is the 3597 test misses (activations 0.01-0.07 of max), as the explanation says.

There is one small systematic false-positive class: when L == 3 and recall_idx == 2, which is the final copy step, all 121 test false positives come from it (precision 0.74 on that subset). Excluding it raises precision to 0.9998 but slightly lowers F1 (0.944), so the original predicate stays. This edge case is minor and the explanation does not mention it.
No systematic gap remains apart from the weak recall_idx 3 tail, which is documented. The label matches the predicate.
